subject.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values

question: Which permanent architecture and canonical PR should own richer config-validation diagnostics: parser-owned source metadata, this PR's display-time JSON5 navigator, or the narrower bracket-only implementation?
rationale: All three user-facing improvements are useful, but choosing a parallel parser versus canonical parse-time provenance affects long-term config ownership, include support, and which overlapping contributor branch should land.

options.title: Canonical parser metadata
options.body: Add source-file and offset provenance to the canonical config parsing/include pipeline, then adapt this PR's formatter and redaction work to consume it.

options.title: Accept the local navigator
options.body: Rebase and land this PR while explicitly accepting its supported JSON5 subset and graceful location loss for included or unsupported syntax.

options.title: Land bracket formatting only
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104935 for the narrow readability fix and defer received values and source locations to a separately designed change.

recommendation.title: Canonical parser metadata
recommendation.body: Add source-file and offset provenance to the canonical config parsing/include pipeline, then adapt this PR's formatter and redaction work to consume it.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to config-validation policy and canonical path behavior.
